findings.issue: ThroughWebViewAsync (lines 70-127) drives the application's own live engine: `_webView()` is `MainWindow.Engine`, i.e. the CoreWebView2 of the running BlazorWebView (src/Wakeel.Desktop/MainWindow.xaml.cs:28,47). `view.NavigateToString(html)` unloads the whole Blazor app, and the `finally` block's `view.Navigate(current)` reloads it from scratch. Every screen's component state is destroyed. Failure scenario: on a machine without Word (the only machine where this path runs at all), the user is standing in the outgoing-letter wizard, presses «حفظ PDF»; the window visibly flashes to a bare letter and back, the app restarts at that route, and everything typed but not yet persisted in the wizard is gone. Word being absent is the exact state the whole fallback exists for, and this path has no automated coverage.
findings.fix: Never touch `window.Engine`. Build a private off-screen engine for the print: `await CoreWebView2Environment.CreateAsync(userDataFolder: <installation staging subfolder>)`, then `CreateCoreWebView2ControllerAsync(hwnd)` on a hidden zero-size HWND (or a `WebView2` control inside a hidden `Window` that is never shown), `NavigateToString(html)`, await `NavigationCompleted`, `PrintToPdfStreamAsync(settings)`, then dispose the controller in a `finally`. Drop the `view.Source` save/restore entirely.

findings.issue: Supervisor ruling (1) for this round: Core-layer Arabic strings belong to CoreAr (ARCHITECTURE §12). LetterAr is still a separate `public static class LetterAr`. src/Wakeel.Core/Services/CoreAr.cs:31 is still `public static class CoreAr` (not partial). Failure scenario: the ratified §12 rule says a reviewer can read every Arabic sentence Core can emit in one place; with LetterAr separate, the letter package's twenty-odd sentences are invisible to that read, and the next package that emits letter text has no single place to look.
findings.fix: Change src/Wakeel.Core/Services/CoreAr.cs:31 to `public static partial class CoreAr` (the partial keyword only — explicitly permitted this round). Move the contents of LetterAr into a new src/Wakeel.Core/Services/Correspondence/CoreAr.Letter.cs as `public static partial class CoreAr { public static class Letter { ... } }` (namespace Wakeel.Core.Services), delete LetterAr.cs, and update the callers: LetterComposer.cs:71, LetterHtmlRenderer.cs:81, DerivedDocumentBuilder.cs:70,76,79,84,234, LetterContracts.cs:486,541 (XML doc crefs), and the tests TemplateServiceTests.cs, DerivedDocumentBuilderTests.cs, LetterComposerTests.cs.

findings.issue: `PrintToPdfStreamAsync(null)` (line 99) prints with WebView2's default print settings — a US-Letter page (8.5 x 11 in) with non-zero margins. Chromium ignores the `@page { size: 210mm 297mm }` rule that LetterHtmlRenderer.Style writes (LetterHtmlRenderer.cs:228) unless the print settings themselves carry the size, and `ILetterPdfWriter.ToPdfAsync` (LetterContracts.cs:515) has no page-size parameter at all, so the writer could not honour it even if it wanted to. Failure scenario: on a Word-less machine an approved A4 letter is saved as PDF; the `.sheet` is 210 mm wide on a 215.9 mm page whose printable width is reduced by the default margins, so the letterhead block is clipped at the edge or spills onto a second page, and an A5 letter is printed on a Letter sheet with two thirds of it blank. The spec row requires the fallback rendering to carry A4/A5.
findings.fix: Add `LetterPageSize pageSize` to `ILetterPdfWriter.ToPdfAsync` and pass `letter.PageSize` from the caller. In ThroughWebViewAsync build `var settings = view.Environment.CreatePrintSettings();` and set `PageWidth`/`PageHeight` to 8.27/11.69 (A4) or 5.83/8.27 (A5) inches, `MarginTop = MarginBottom = MarginLeft = MarginRight = 0`, `ShouldPrintBackgrounds = true`, then `PrintToPdfStreamAsync(settings)`. Assert the page size in a test over the settings object built by a small pure helper.

findings.issue: Run() (lines 133-180) creates Word and calls `Documents.Open` with no macro guard: `AutomationSecurity` is never set, so Word opens the file with the machine's normal macro trust. The spec's security check requires no macro execution and no external relationships followed. LetterComposer.Compose copies the office's template package verbatim (LetterComposer.cs:44-53) and TemplateService.CheckAsync accepts any package the OpenXML SDK can open (TemplateService.cs:87-96) — it screens size only. Failure scenario: an office uploads a template that carries `w:attachedTemplate` in word/settings.xml pointing at a .dotm on a share (an external relationship), or a macro-enabled package saved under a .docx name. Every generated letter inherits it, and the moment «تحرير في Word» or the Word PDF export opens that letter, Word loads the attached template and its AutoOpen/AutoNew macros run under the user's account. Nothing in the package looks for either.
findings.fix: In WordSession.Run, immediately after `dynamic word = application;` and before `Documents.Open`, set `word.AutomationSecurity = 3;` (msoAutomationSecurityForceDisable) inside the existing try. Additionally, in TemplateService.CheckAsync/SaveLocalCopyAsync reject a package that (a) declares a main-part content type other than application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document.main+xml, (b) contains an entry named word/vbaProject.bin, or (c) carries any relationship with TargetMode="External" in word/_rels/document.xml.rels or word/_rels/settings.xml.rels — returning LetterTemplateCheck.Unreadable with the existing LetterAr.TemplateUnreadable sentence.

findings.issue: MergeRuns (lines 88-138) iterates `paragraph.Elements<Run>()`, which is direct children only, while TextOf/OwnTexts (lines 73-79) read every Text whose nearest Paragraph ancestor is this paragraph — including runs nested inside a Hyperlink, SimpleField, SdtRun or InsertedRun. The two views disagree. Failure scenario: a letterhead paragraph shaped [Run "البريد "][Hyperlink[Run "info@x.gov"]][Run " هاتف 011"] where the two outer runs share identical rPr: MergeRuns appends the third run's text onto the first and removes the third, so the paragraph now reads «البريد هاتف 011 info@x.gov» in the generated letter. The joined text the mark search and Splice index against is reordered along with it, so a mark that straddled the hyperlink is spliced at the wrong offset.
findings.fix: Walk `paragraph.ChildElements` rather than `paragraph.Elements<Run>()`, and reset `previous`/`previousProperties` to null on every child that is not a `Run` except the harmless markers (BookmarkStart, BookmarkEnd, ProofError, CommentRangeStart/End, ParagraphProperties). Two runs then merge only when nothing that can carry text sits between them.

findings.issue: ReferralTo (line 87), ReferralDue (line 91) and PageSize (line 95) interpolate values straight into an Arabic sentence with no bidi isolate, while every comparable sentence in the same layer uses CoreAr.Isolate (CoreAr.cs:162,177,187,204,447,449,472,476 — the convention is documented at CoreAr.cs:499-503 as "the isolate has to travel with the text" because these strings are stored and printed, not wrapped in a <bdi> by a screen). Failure scenario: `ReferralTo("مكتب IT الداخلي")` yields «إلى: مكتب IT الداخلي»; the Latin run and the neutral colon resolve against the surrounding RTL context and the colon can be laid out at the wrong end of the line. These strings are written into a saved .docx (DerivedDocumentBuilder.Lines/Line, lines 74-99 and 217-220), so the wrong order is printed on an official copy and cannot be fixed afterwards. `PageSize` has the same problem with the literal "A4"/"A5" beside a parenthesised Arabic phrase.
findings.fix: Use the existing helper: `$"إلى: {CoreAr.Isolate(toAr)}"`, `$"المهلة: {CoreAr.Isolate(dateAr)}"`, and `size == LetterPageSize.A5 ? $"{CoreAr.Isolate("A5")} (نصف صفحة)" : $"{CoreAr.Isolate("A4")} (صفحة كاملة)"`. Do this in the same change that folds these strings into CoreAr.

findings.issue: Bidi() (line 219) is applied to a whole already-filled template line (line 65: `Bidi(Fill(line, values))`), so the single <bdi> isolates the line from its siblings but leaves each substituted value un-isolated inside it. The class remark at lines 22-25 claims "every one is wrapped so that Arabic and Latin text on one line ... stays in the order it was typed", and LetterHtmlRendererTests.The_rendering_is_right_to_left_and_isolates_every_value asserts only that the literal strings "<bdi>" and "unicode-bidi: isolate" occur somewhere in the page — it would pass unchanged if no value were isolated at all. Failure scenario: the template line «الرقم / @رقم الصادر   التاريخ / @التاريخ الهجري» renders as one bdi; a number such as «WM-2026/14» beside the Arabic label resolves under the surrounding paragraph direction rather than on its own, and the slash/hyphen can be laid out on the wrong side. Practically mitigated by `.line { unicode-bidi: plaintext }`, but not by what the comment and test claim.
findings.fix: Split each template line at its mark boundaries in Render (the substitution already knows where they are) and emit `<bdi>` around the substituted value only, leaving the template's own fixed text outside it — the same way AppendSpans already does per span. Then strengthen the test to assert the concrete substring, e.g. that the rendered number appears as `<bdi>و/م/1448/214</bdi>` rather than merely that some <bdi> exists.

findings.issue: ApplyListLook line 223 sets `properties.Justification = new Justification { Val = JustificationValues.Both }` (fully justified, both margins) directly beneath the comment at lines 221-222 that says "A list item is never justified: stretching an item to both margins pulls its words away from its marker." The code does the exact thing the comment forbids. Failure scenario: a numbered body item shorter than a full line is stretched to both margins, so «1.» sits at the right margin with a wide gap before its text — the layout the author documented as wrong — on every A4 letter that carries a list.
findings.fix: Set `JustificationValues.Start`, or drop the Justification override entirely and let the item inherit the template paragraph's own alignment (which is what the cloned modelProperties already carries). Add an assertion in LetterComposerTests.Compose_writes_paragraphs_lists_and_bold that the list paragraph's Justification is not Both.

findings.issue: ReanchorVmlStyle (lines 241-271) rewrites the VML fallback shape's `mso-position-horizontal-relative`/`mso-position-vertical-relative` from page to margin but never adjusts the shape's `left:`/`top:` declarations, whereas the DrawingML path does subtract the margin from PositionOffset (ReanchorHorizontal line 204, ReanchorVertical line 228). The builder's report claims both copies are rewritten; only one is rewritten correctly. Failure scenario: a template whose letterhead text box says `position:absolute;left:56.7pt;top:56.7pt;mso-position-horizontal-relative:page` becomes margin-relative with left/top unchanged, so in a Word old enough to render mc:Fallback the box is displaced by one full margin (about 2 cm) down and across on every letter.
findings.fix: In the same loop, parse the `left` and `top` declarations (values carry a pt/in/cm suffix), subtract the margin converted to that unit, and write them back — mirroring ReanchorHorizontal/ReanchorVertical. If a unit cannot be parsed, leave that shape's relative declaration as `page` rather than moving it, so the fallback is never silently displaced.

findings.issue: The body pass (lines 102-119) re-reads the paragraph and searches for LetterMarks.Body again after LetterBodyWriter.Insert has written into it, guarded only by `while (guard++ < 4)`. Nothing prevents the inserted content from containing the mark. Failure scenario: the head of office types «أرفقنا نموذجًا يوضح موضع @نص المراسلة في القالب» in the internal editor; that text is inserted, the loop finds the mark inside it, and the entire body is spliced in again — four times before the guard stops it. The same happens through data: SimpleValues is applied first, so a subject or office name containing the literal mark makes the whole letter body be inserted into the subject line.
findings.fix: Insert once per paragraph: replace the `while (guard++ < 4)` loop with a single `if (at >= 0) LetterBodyWriter.Insert(...)`, and have Insert return the last paragraph it produced so a template with a second body mark further down is still reached by the outer `foreach` (which already iterates a snapshot taken before insertion).

findings.issue: Two problems in the bullet definition. (a) Abstract() line 119/131 pairs `LevelText { Val = "•" }` (U+2022) with `RunFonts { Ascii = "Symbol", HighAnsi = "Symbol" }`; Word's own convention is either LevelText "" with the Symbol font or U+2022 with an ordinary text font, so Word is asked to look U+2022 up in a symbol-encoded font and the printed marker may not be a bullet. (b) Ensure() lines 65-66 `PrependChild` the new w:abstractNum at the head of w:numbering, which places them before any `w:numPicBullet` the office's template carries; CT_Numbering requires every numPicBullet to precede every abstractNum, so such a template produces a letter Word reports as corrupt. Failure scenario: an office template that uses a picture bullet anywhere; the first letter with a bulleted body opens with Word's repair prompt.
findings.fix: (a) Use `LevelText { Val = "" }` together with the Symbol RunFonts. (b) Insert the two abstract definitions after the last existing `w:numPicBullet` (`numbering.Elements<NumberingPictureBullet>().LastOrDefault()` → `InsertAfter`, falling back to PrependChild when there is none) instead of unconditionally at the head.

findings.issue: Both tests "skip" by writing an Arabic sentence to ITestOutputHelper and returning (lines 23-33 and 74-84). xUnit records them as passing. Failure scenario: on a build agent without Word, the run reports two green tests that asserted nothing and the reason is visible only if somebody opens that test's captured output — exactly the silent-pass the package instructions rule out ("tests that skip must say why"). The second test is already a permanent no-op on this machine, where Word is installed.
findings.fix: Use the runner's skip mechanism so the reason lands in the run summary: `Assert.Skip("Word غير مثبّت على هذا الجهاز")` on xunit.v3, or add a `[SkippableFact]`/`Skip.If(!WordSession.IsAvailable, "...")` helper if this project is still on xunit v2 (the same helper the OCR/model tests will need).

missing_spec_items: Review check (3), "no macro execution, no external relationships followed": nothing in the package enforces this on the Word side. TemplateService.CheckAsync screens size only, and WordSession opens the generated letter with Word's normal macro trust (no AutomationSecurity), so a macro-enabled package or a w:attachedTemplate external relationship in an office-supplied template survives Compose into every letter and is honoured when Word opens it. See finding 4.

Spec row "توليد PDF عبر Word أو WebView2.PrintToPdf بديلًا ... A4/A5": the WebView2 fallback does not carry the letter's page size. ILetterPdfWriter.ToPdfAsync takes no LetterPageSize and PrintToPdfStreamAsync is called with null settings, so the fallback PDF comes out on WebView2's default (US-Letter) page regardless of what the wizard chose. See finding 3.
Supervisor ruling (1) of this round is not carried out: LetterAr is still a separate class rather than part of CoreAr. See finding 2.

WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD, and I checked it rather than took it on trust.

Conformance is real. LetterConformanceTests composes from docs/templates/correspondence/نموذج-المراسلة.docx with the owner's own values and compares Meaningful(ReadLines(...)) against his hand-filled مثال-مراسلة-المالك.docx, paragraph for paragraph over every part, whitespace collapsed — and it passes. The «19 صفر 1448» / «2 أغسطس 2026» assertion pins the UmAlQura conversion and both sets of Arabic month names to the owner's own handwriting rather than to the code's opinion. LetterDates correctly uses UmAlQuraCalendar (not HijriCalendar), returns empty outside the tables, and formats through InvariantCulture so item 20's western digits cannot be undone by the thread's culture.

The cross-run splice in LetterOpenXml is the right design and is proven: Compose_sees_a_mark_that_Word_cut_into_pieces uses a template whose mark is stored as three runs. Both text-box copies are reached (Compose_replaces_marks_inside_text_boxes_in_both_copies asserts the number and the sender each appear at least twice — the mc:Choice drawing and the mc:Fallback VML). The header is covered. A5 sets pgSz to 8419x11906 and LetterProbe.PageAnchoredShapes comes back empty, so nothing is left tied to the paper. Compose_never_changes_the_template_it_was_given proves the caller's bytes are untouched. LetterProbe's assertions are real inspections of the OpenXML tree (bold is read off RunProperties.Bold, numbering is matched against the ids actually declared in the part), not string matching on the docx. The Word COM test does run for real here — it produced a non-empty PDF and WordProcessesLeftBehind confirms WINWORD exited within 20 s.

Files are written under the installation folders only: WordAutomation stages in paths.StagingDir (WakeelPaths.cs:47, under Root) and TemplateService writes Root\\templates\\letter-template.docx temp-then-move. DI resolves: WakeelPaths is registered by AddWakeelCore (ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:40) and the optional ILetterDocumentStore parameter is satisfied by its default value, so TemplateService constructs even before B3-2 lands. No new NuGet package; Directory.Build.props, Directory.Packages.props, Wakeel.slnx and docs/ (bar the progress file) are untouched — the only csproj edits are the permitted ProjectReference and the EmbeddedResource.

RULINGS I APPLIED AS TOLD, and did not reopen: WordSession living in Wakeel.Reports (2), the tests living in Wakeel.Core.Tests with the docx embedded from its docs/ path (3), LetterPageFit being an estimate (4), and the PrintToPdf fallback having no automated test (5). None of my findings contradicts those. Finding 1 is about what that untested fallback *does* to the running application, which ruling (5) does not cover; finding 3 is about the page size it prints on, likewise.

ON LetterPageFit, since ruling (4) requires it to err toward an added page: it mostly does — an exactly-full page yields FreeOnLastPageTwips = 0 and therefore an added page, and the caller is told which case was chosen through DerivedDocumentResult.ExtraPageAdded/NoticeAr, with PreviewAsync giving the same answer before saving (tested). One soft spot worth knowing rather than fixing now: Measure (LetterPageFit.cs:98-101) falls back to `used % contentHeight` whenever the body contains any explicit page break, but `used` never accounts for the break itself, so for a document that breaks early the remainder is unrelated to what is actually on the last page and can read optimistically. It cannot arise from a letter this package composes (Compose emits no page breaks), only from a document a future package hands the builder. Calibrating this against real printed letters during the B3 walkthrough, as the builder suggested, is the right moment to tighten it.

VERDICT is fix, on four mediums and one high. The high (finding 1) and finding 3 are the two that change what an office actually gets on paper when Word is absent, and they sit in the same method — fix them together. Finding 2 is the supervisor's ruling and is a mechanical change. Findings 4 and 5 are small, well-localised edits. The low findings are worth doing in the same pass but none of them blocks the package.
